title: Assassination
text: “How am I supposed to sleep in a bed this lousy?!”

Smoked Meat is complaining about the bed and venting his frustration at the servants. He’s been acting all high and mighty ever since before he even met Itsuki. Come to think of it, I seem to recall him bragging about his family background when he introduced himself… I’d tuned him out, figuring a guy’s background didn’t matter, so I’d forgotten all about it.

But this Smoked Meat… he was the ringleader of all the trouble in the future, wasn’t he? If I recall correctly, in the future, he foolishly conspired with the Crimson Swine and the Three Heroes Church to stage a revolution against the country and his Father. I wasn’t actually there, so I don’t know the details, but I heard he hurled some pretty harsh insults at his Father.

What should we do? Would taking him out here have a major impact on the future? …I get the feeling there wouldn’t be any problem in eliminating this potential threat. Just like with Takt, I actually think it might work to our advantage. But it’d be a hassle if any witnesses showed up.
Just as I’m thinking that, he gives the soldiers an order regarding the bed and walks off somewhere. Where on earth is he going?
“The Love Hunter, the Source of All Power, commands: Interpret the truth once more, and conceal your form with a Fire Mirage.”
“Drifa Fire Mirage”

It’s not quite as good as my sister-in-law’s, but I’ll use a variation of fire magic to hide myself. Since I also have a skill called “Cloaking Lance,” I’ll use them together—I think I’ve managed to hide myself completely. Of course, I’ll boost my weapon to Rank X. Otherwise, since I cast the spell so forcefully, I’d be as obvious as day.
I keep following Smoked Meat right behind him. As for witnesses… there don’t seem to be any so far.
“Tch! I’m running low on booze.”

Muttering to himself, the Smoked Meat appears to be heading toward the castle’s wine cellar. Is he planning to use his family’s status as a shield to sneak a drink? Just as he reached the courtyard on his way to the castle’s warehouse, I took a wide detour to get ahead of him. A ceiling would make things tricky due to range limitations. But if I fired horizontally, I might end up damaging the building.
He’s clattering along with a confident stride. There’s no one else around. Now’s my chance! I… grabbed Smoked Meat’s collar with all my strength.
“Huh!? N-nothing—”
I yanked him toward me with all my might, flung him upward, and thrust my spear toward Smoked Meat.
“Guaaaaah!”

Once I confirmed the spear had pierced him with a *thud*, I unleashed my skill. In Brionac, a beam of light shooting into the sky might give me away. But then again, the Meteor Thrust would do the same… Hmm, I never thought the day would come when I’d have to agonize over which killing skill to use. I guess this is the one.
“Burst Lance X!”
It’s a skill that blows up the target I’ve pierced, so I blew the Smoked Meat to smithereens.
“Ah—”
The sound of the explosion echoed throughout the area.
“W-what!?”

Soldiers rushed over at the noise, but I immediately went into hiding and moved on. Besides, since I blew it away without leaving a corpse, it’d be hard for them to figure out what happened based on anything other than the sound. In fact, even the soldiers heard the noise but couldn’t quite figure out what had happened. They walked off in the completely wrong direction.
“Hahaha, so that’s one… piece of trash in this world gone.”
Since there’s not a trace left behind, it might actually be better than trash. I never thought I’d be able to get rid of this guy so quickly. I’m actually pretty lucky, aren’t I?

Now for the Crimson Swine… but I still have a job for him to do. If I were to kill the Crimson Swine right now, it would make a huge difference in the future. I’d better think carefully about the right timing to kill him, too.
Ah, Filolial-sama! I got a bit carried away trying to get rid of the trash and it took me a while, but I’m heading over right now.
“Gua-gua”
When I popped my head into Filolial-sama’s quarters, he seemed to be snoring away as usual. Just like the first time I looped, I offered food to Filolial-sama and the others to win their favor.
The next morning, I woke up at the Filolial Lodge and headed straight to meet up with my Father and the others.
“Kitamura-kun, where did you go in the middle of the night? Don’t you smell a little funny?”
“I went to see Filolial-sama. My Father’s daughter, Filo-tan, is also a Filolial.”
But I’d like to correct one thing. Filolial-sama actually has a noble scent.
“Filolial-sama?”
“It’s a bird-like monster that pulls a carriage.”
The minister who was guiding us added.
“Ah… so that’s it. Am I supposed to marry a bird monster!?”
My Father nodded, as if he understood. Oh! So he actually believed what I was saying.
“Kitamura-kun, your jokes are going too far… A man taking a wife, and on top of that, marrying a bird that pulls a carriage? You really should go see a doctor.”
My father is saying something that makes him seem even more distant than before. Hmm… I thought carefully before speaking—what’s so wrong with what I said?
“This guy seems a bit off his rocker, so it’s best not to engage with him.”
“You’re right.”
“Well… since he’s one of our fellow heroes, let’s at least talk to him a little. Otherwise, it’d be a shame, wouldn’t it? He’s good-looking, after all.”
My father came to my defense. This Motoyasu—tears are streaming down his face and won’t stop.
“He’s started crying like a waterfall. What happened?”
“I told you, there’s something a little off about this guy.”
“He’d be a total heartthrob if he’d just keep his mouth shut. What a waste, Motoyasu Kitamura.”
“The Hero has arrived.”
When we reached the throne room, the pig and the men were waiting for us. Eleven of them in all. Haha, my actions have certainly borne fruit.
“I put out a call for anyone who wanted to join the Hero on his journey following yesterday’s incident. It seems everyone here has a Hero they’d like to accompany.”
My Father muttered this while quietly raising his hand to block the sound from reaching me and Ren.
“Eleven people… even if we split them three ways, isn’t that one person short?”
Ren and Itsuki nodded in agreement. But I know better. Even if there were twelve of them, my Father wouldn’t be able to gather any companions. So the actual number is meaningless.
To begin with, among the folks who joined us here… was there even anyone who stuck around until the very end? Unfortunately, I don’t recall any. Come to think of it, why isn’t it up to us to choose?
We’re the ones summoned to save the world as Heroes. Shouldn’t the country that summoned us show some sincerity? Just thinking that made me feel a surge of murderous intent toward Trash.
“Now then, future heroes. Set out on your journey with the Hero you wish to serve.”
It feels like we’re being forced to watch a blatantly staged farce. My Father and the others look completely dumbfounded, too. Eleven potential companions are shuffling over toward us.
Ren: five. Itsuki, three. Me, three. Father, zero.
“Hey, Your Majesty!”

The numbers are close to what they were the first time around. It’s only natural that Father would be dissatisfied! I could fly into a rage right here, but I’m holding it in because of what my future Father said.

That Trash—even though it was decided from the start—is putting on a dramatic act and wiping the sweat from his face. If he’s that worked up, maybe I’ll make him break out in a cold sweat in an instant?
“U-uh. I must admit, even I never imagined a situation like this would arise.”
“You lack the support of the people, don’t you?”
At the muttered words of that minister-like guy, I felt a surge of murderous intent and pointed my spear at him.
“You’d better stop this farce. Such blatant discrimination… I find it highly offensive.”
It shouldn’t be a problem to say something like this, right?
“N-no… my apologies.”
Just as the minister apologized, that wizard-like guy standing next to Trash whispered.
“Hmm, so rumors like that are spreading…”
How insincere… At that moment, I asked in polite language what had happened, but when I showed my displeasure and fell silent, Itsuki stepped forward and asked.
“Is something wrong?”
My Father was nodding his head repeatedly, seemingly unable to accept the situation.
“Hmm, actually… it seems a rumor is spreading among the Heroes that the Shield Hero is the weakest of them all.”
“Huh!?”
“According to legend, they’re all supposed to be strong, but I doubt many would want to travel with a weak Hero.”
Huh? In the previous loop, they excluded him because he lacked knowledge. This time, it’s for a different reason.

But either way, listening to this farce is pushing my patience to the limit. There’s no way my weak Father could defeat the Pope or the Spirit Tortoise. He’s actually incredibly strong. The more I think about it, the more full of contradictions this whole thing is.
“No… that kind of talk… did you hear about what happened last night?”
